question: What should the first OpenClaw-owned skill permission manifest contract include, and how should declared permissions relate to install consent, audit/trust scoring, signing, attestation, ClawHub verification, and runtime enforcement?
rationale: This defines a public ecosystem contract and security boundary; automation cannot safely choose schema placement, trust roots, consent semantics, or enforcement timing from source inspection alone.

options.title: Consolidate Design First
options.body: Keep this issue open as the product/security design anchor and use the related RFCs, plugins, forks, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95220 as input before accepting a public manifest contract.

options.title: Land Audit-Only Metadata First
options.body: Adopt a narrow optional manifest that is explicitly inspect-only, then track consent, signing, attestation, and enforcement as separate phases.

options.title: Route Trust Scoring To ClawHub
options.body: Let ClawHub or external governance plugins own declarations and trust scoring unless a missing core API is identified.

recommendation.title: Consolidate Design First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the product/security design anchor and use the related RFCs, plugins, forks, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95220 as input before accepting a public manifest contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the visible product/security reviewer for this issue and have recent skills documentation and hook-surface history.
